blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Twenty charging points were added across the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) amid a growing number of electric and hybrid vehicles, its operator announced Friday. According to NLEX Corp. in a statement, six of its service stops have been equipped with 20 EV charging points as of November 2026. READ: Toll board orders NLEx operator to address flooding in Pampanga These facilities, said the corporation, provide power ratings ranging from 22 kilowatt (kW) to 240 kW. “NLEX Corporation is responding to this shift by expanding the availability of electric vehicle charging facilities along its expressway network, giving EV owners […]...
